'''Richmond Sarpong''' (born April 23, 1974, in [[Bechem]], [[Ghana]])<ref name=":5" /> is a Ghanaian-American chemist who is the [[Henry Rapoport]] Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Richmond Sarpong {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://sarponggroup.com/richmond-sarpong/ |access-date=2021-05-31 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> Sarpong works on [[natural product]] [[total synthesis]] to better understand biological systems and allow for the development of novel therapeutics. He was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 2017,<ref name=":4" /> and was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Richmond Sarpong|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/richmond-sarpong|access-date=2021-05-31|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> and to the [[National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Science]] in 2025.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |title=Richmond Sarpong elected to National Academy of Sciences {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/richmond-sarpong-elected-national-academy-sciences |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> He serves on the editorial boards of ''[[Organic Syntheses]], [[Accounts of Chemical Research]]'' and ''[[Synlett]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OrgSyn Board|url=http://www.orgsyn.org/BOE.aspx?show=B|access-date=2020-08-13|website=www.orgsyn.org}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Sarpong was born in [[Bechem]], [[Ghana]] on April 23, 1974, and spent his early childhood in [[Bolgatanga]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Organic Chemistry Seminar: Professor Richmond Sarpong, University of California, Berkeley {{!}} Department of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.stanford.edu/events/organic-chemistry-seminar-professor-richmond-sarpong-university-california-berkeley|access-date=2020-08-13|website=chemistry.stanford.edu}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|date=2019|title=Richmond Sarpong|journal=ChemCatChem|volume=11|issue=13|pages=2942|doi=10.1002/cctc.201900804|issn=1867-3899|doi-access=free}}</ref> His mother is a teacher, and his father a medical doctor who also holds a master's degree in public health.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Reactions – Richmond Sarpong : The Sceptical Chymist|url=http://blogs.nature.com/thescepticalchymist/2009/06/reactions_richmond_sarpong.html|access-date=2020-08-13|website=blogs.nature.com}}</ref> It was during his childhood that Sarpong first became interested in chemistry, when he saw how effective the drug [[ivermectin]] was in combatting [[river blindness]] (''[[onchocerciasis]]'').<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Drahl|first=Carmen|title=Why The 2015 Nobel Prize In Medicine Was The Boyhood Inspiration For A Chemist From Africa|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/carmendrahl/2015/10/05/why-the-2015-nobel-prize-in-medicine-was-the-boyhood-inspiration-for-a-chemist-from-africa/|access-date=2020-08-13|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref> Ivermectin was being distributed in Africa by [[Merck & Co.|Merck]] free of charge,<ref>{{Cite news |author=<!--Not stated-->|date=1987-10-22|title=Merck Offers Free Distribution of New River Blindness Drug|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/10/22/world/merck-offers-free-distribution-of-new-river-blindness-drug.html|access-date=2021-05-31|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and Sarpong's father worked with the [[World Health Organization]] to aid in the distribution of the drug.<ref name=":2" /> Sarpong got his hands on his father's copy of the [[Merck Index]], an encyclopedia of chemicals, and spent his free time imagining how chemistry could change people's lives. In 1984, Sarpong's family moved to [[Livingstone, Zambia|Livingstone]], [[Zambia]] and later [[Lobatse]], [[Botswana]] in 1986. In Zambia and Botswana, he saw the devastating impact of [[HIV/AIDS in Africa]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Faculty Mentor Richmond Sarpong Supports His Amgen Scholars|url=https://amgenscholars.com/faculty-mentor-richmond-sarpong-supports-his-amgen-scholars/|access-date=2020-08-13|website=Amgen Scholars|language=en-US}}</ref> In Botswana, Sarpong attended the [[Maru-a-Pula School]], where he was introduced to organic chemistry by his teacher Dr. Ramakrishna.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web|last=Drahl|first=Carmen|date=March 9, 2015|title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar Awards|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i10/Arthur-C-Cope-Scholar-Awards.html?type=paidArticleContent|access-date=2021-05-31|website=cen.acs.org}}</ref> Having this additional mentor encouraged Sarpong to pursue a career in chemistry, despite having an offer from a premedical program at a British university.<ref name=":8" />

== Education and training ==
Sarpong moved to the [[United States]] in 1991 to study chemistry at [[Macalester College]]. At Macalester, he conducted undergraduate research with Prof. [[Rebecca Hoye|Rebecca C. Hoye]] on the determination of [[Absolute configuration|absolute stereochemistry]] of organic molecules using the [https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2007.354 Mosher method].<ref name=":5" /> Sarpong graduated with his B.A. in chemistry in 1995.

Sarpong then pursued graduate studies with Prof. [[Martin Semmelhack]] at [[Princeton University]]. In Prof. Semmelhack's laboratory, he worked on organic compounds containing the [[enediyne]] functional group that model the activity of the [[calicheamicin]] class of antibiotics.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Semmelhack|first1=M. F.|last2=Sarpong|first2=R.|date=2004|title=Kinetic analysis of a reactive model enediyne|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/poc.798|journal=Journal of Physical Organic Chemistry|language=en|volume=17|issue=9|pages=807–813|doi=10.1002/poc.798|issn=1099-1395|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=2002-01-21|title=Evaluation of alkene isomerization as a trigger for enediyne activation|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0040403901021396|journal=Tetrahedron Letters|language=en|volume=43|issue=4|pages=541–544|doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)02139-6|issn=0040-4039|last1=Semmelhack|first1=M.F.|last2=Sarpong|first2=Richmond|last3=Bergman|first3=Jeffrey|last4=Ho|first4=Douglas M.|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Sarpong received his Ph.D. in 2001.

Sarpong moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] where he joined the laboratory of Prof. [[Brian Stoltz]] as a [[UNCF]]-[[Pfizer]] Postdoctoral fellow. At Caltech, he worked alongside then-graduate student [[Neil Garg]] to complete the first total synthesis of the phosphate inhibitor dragmacidin D.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Garg|first1=Neil K.|last2=Sarpong|first2=Richmond|last3=Stoltz|first3=Brian M.|date=2002-11-01|title=The First Total Synthesis of Dragmacidin D|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja027822b|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=124|issue=44|pages=13179–13184|doi=10.1021/ja027822b|pmid=12405846|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Sarpong also developed a novel [[Tandem reaction|tandem]] [[Wolff rearrangement|Wolff]]/[[Cope rearrangement]] to synthesize fused ring molecules.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sarpong|first1=Richmond|last2=Su|first2=Julius T.|last3=Stoltz|first3=Brian M.|date=2003|title=The Development of a Facile Tandem Wolff/Cope Rearrangement for the Synthesis of Fused Carbocyclic Skeletons|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja037587c|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=125|issue=45|pages=13624–13625|doi=10.1021/ja037587c|pmid=14599176|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 2004, Sarpong started his independent scientific career at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as an assistant professor.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2018-03-29|title=Strategies and Methods for Chemical Synthesis Inspired by Natural Products|url=https://chem.columbia.edu/events/colloquia/strategies-methods-chemical-synthesis-inspired-natural-products/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Columbia University}}</ref> He was promoted to associate professor in 2010 and full Professor in 2014.

The Sarpong group specialize in the synthesis of bioactive organic molecules, with a focus on the [[natural product]]s of flora and fauna.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Richmond Sarpong|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/richmond-sarpong/|access-date=2020-08-13|language=en-US}}</ref> He has developed new synthesis strategies for [[alkaloid]]s, a family of natural medicines that includes quinine and morphine.<ref name=":2" /> In particular, Sarpong is interested in natural product synthesis for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.<ref name=":3" />

In 2017, Sarpong delivered a talk at [[TED (conference)|TEDx]] Berkeley entitled ''The face of disease in Sub-Saharan Africa'', in which described the influences on his desire to pursue chemistry growing up in Africa, and also encouraged his audience to reevaluate their perceptions of disease in Africa.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=The face of disease in Sub-Saharan Africa {{!}} Richmond Sarpong {{!}} TEDxBerkeley {{!}} College of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/file/face-disease-sub-saharan-africa-richmond-sarpong-tedxberkeley|access-date=2020-08-13|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=TEDxBerkeley |url=https://www.ted.com/tedx/events/12582|access-date=2020-08-13|website=www.ted.com}}</ref> Sarpong is committed to improving diversity within the chemistry community,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Reisman|first1=Sarah E.|last2=Sarpong|first2=Richmond|last3=Sigman|first3=Matthew S.|last4=Yoon|first4=Tehshik P.|date=2020-08-21|title=Organic Chemistry: A Call to Action for Diversity and Inclusion|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=85|issue=16|pages=10287–10292|doi=10.1021/acs.joc.0c01607|pmid=32806096|s2cid=221165007|issn=0022-3263|doi-access=free}}</ref> and has supported many scholars in the early stages of their academic careers.<ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
Sarpong plays tennis in his free time.<ref name=":8" /> While attending Macalester College as an undergraduate, he set the 100-meter dash record.<ref name=":8" />

Sarpong's sister, Martha Sarpong, is a R&D Director and Project Leader at [[GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals Ltd|GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals]].<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Martha Sarpong '97, PhD|url=https://www.macalester.edu/theolinricehub/marthasarpong/|access-date=2021-05-31|language=en-US}}</ref>
